mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the diagnostic floral characters of the Fabaceae, Solanaceae and Liliaceae families?

options.A: Fabaceae: zygomorphic, papilionaceous flower with banner, wings, keel; Solanaceae: actinomorphic, pentamerous, fused corolla; Liliaceae: trimerous, six tepals, superior ovary.
options.B: Fabaceae: actinomorphic, radial symmetry; Solanaceae: zygomorphic, bilabiate; Liliaceae: pentamerous, fused petals.
options.C: Fabaceae: trimerous, six tepals; Solanaceae: monocot, parallel veins; Liliaceae: dicot, netted veins.
options.D: Fabaceae: compound leaves with stipules; Solanaceae: simple leaves; Liliaceae: whorled leaves.

mcqs.answer: Fabaceae: zygomorphic, papilionaceous flower with banner, wings, keel; Solanaceae: actinomorphic, pentamerous, fused corolla; Liliaceae: trimerous, six tepals, superior ovary.
mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae flowers are typically papilionaceous (zygomorphic) with a banner, wings and keel. Solanaceae flowers are usually actinomorphic, pentamerous and have a fused corolla forming a tube. Liliaceae, being monocots, have trimerous flowers with six tepals and a superior ovary. The other options mix up symmetry, floral part numbers, or vegetative traits, making them incorrect.

mcqs.question: Match the plant with its family and primary economic use: (i) Peanut, (ii) Tomato, (iii) Onion. Which option correctly pairs each plant with its family and a major economic use?

options.A: Peanut – Fabaceae – source of edible oil; Tomato – Solanaceae – vegetable crop; Onion – Liliaceae – spice and vegetable.
options.B: Peanut – Solanaceae – source of edible oil; Tomato – Fabaceae – vegetable crop; Onion – Liliaceae – ornamental.
options.C: Peanut – Fabaceae – ornamental; Tomato – Liliaceae – spice; Onion – Solanaceae – vegetable.
options.D: Peanut – Fabaceae – timber; Tomato – Solanaceae – medicinal; Onion – Liliaceae – fiber.

mcqs.answer: Peanut – Fabaceae – source of edible oil; Tomato – Solanaceae – vegetable crop; Onion – Liliaceae – spice and vegetable.
mcqs.explanation: Peanut belongs to Fabaceae and is cultivated for its oil‑rich seeds. Tomato is a member of Solanaceae and is a major vegetable crop worldwide. Onion is placed in Liliaceae (or the related Amaryllidaceae) and is used both as a spice and a vegetable. The other options assign plants to wrong families or incorrect primary uses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the Fabaceae family?

options.A: Flowers arranged in a papilionaceous (butterfly) shape with banner, wings, and keel.
options.B: Flowers with a superior ovary and six tepals.
options.C: Flowers with fused corolla forming a tube and berry fruit.
options.D: Flowers with numerous stamens and a spadix.

mcqs.answer: Flowers arranged in a papilionaceous (butterfly) shape with banner, wings, and keel.
mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae (legume family) is distinguished by its papilionaceous flower, which is zygomorphic and consists of a large upper petal (banner), two lateral petals (wings) and two lower fused petals forming the keel. Options B, C and D describe traits of other families (Liliaceae, Solanaceae, Araceae respectively).

mcqs.question: A plant has actinomorphic, pentamerous flowers with a superior ovary that develops into a berry, and its leaves are alternate with stipules. To which family does it most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae flowers are typically actinomorphic, pentamerous, and often have a fused corolla forming a tube; the fruit is commonly a berry. Alternate leaves with stipules are also common. Fabaceae have papilionaceous flowers, Liliaceae are monocots with trimerous flowers, and Poaceae are grasses with very different floral structures.

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly distinguishes the Liliaceae family from Fabaceae and Solanaceae?

options.A: Liliaceae are monocotyledonous plants with trimerous flowers having six tepals and superior ovaries, whereas Fabaceae and Solanaceae are dicotyledonous with pentamerous flowers.
options.B: Liliaceae are dicotyledonous with papilionaceous flowers, unlike Fabaceae and Solanaceae.
options.C: Liliaceae have fused petals forming a tube, unlike Fabaceae and Solanaceae.
options.D: Liliaceae produce leguminous pods, unlike Fabaceae and Solanaceae.

mcqs.answer: Liliaceae are monocotyledonous plants with trimerous flowers having six tepals and superior ovaries, whereas Fabaceae and Solanaceae are dicotyledonous with pentamerous flowers.
mcqs.explanation: Liliaceae are true monocots; their flowers are typically trimerous (parts in threes) with six tepals and a superior ovary. Fabaceae and Solanaceae are dicots and generally have pentamerous (five‑part) flowers. Options B, C and D describe incorrect characteristics for Liliaceae.

mcqs.question: A flower observed has five fused petals forming a tube, five stamens attached to the corolla tube, and a superior ovary that develops into a berry. To which family does this flower most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: The described floral structure—actinomorphic, pentamerous, fused corolla forming a tube, five stamens attached to the corolla, and a berry fruit—is characteristic of the Solanaceae family (e.g., tomato, pepper). Fabaceae have papilionaceous flowers, Liliaceae have trimerous flowers, and Asteraceae have composite inflorescences.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly identifies an economically important member of each of the three families?

options.A: Peanut (Fabaceae) – source of oil; Potato (Solanaceae) – staple food; Tulip (Liliaceae) – ornamental flower.
options.B: Soybean (Fabaceae) – timber; Tomato (Solanaceae) – ornamental; Lily (Liliaceae) – edible tuber.
options.C: Lentil (Fabaceae) – spice; Eggplant (Solanaceae) – fiber; Onion (Liliaceae) – medicinal herb.
options.D: Pea (Fabaceae) – ornamental; Bell pepper (Solanaceae) – timber; Garlic (Liliaceae) – oilseed.

mcqs.answer: Peanut (Fabaceae) – source of oil; Potato (Solanaceae) – staple food; Tulip (Liliaceae) – ornamental flower.
mcqs.explanation: Peanut belongs to Fabaceae and is cultivated for its oil‑rich seeds. Potato is a Solanaceous crop that is a global staple food. Tulip, a member of Liliaceae, is widely grown as an ornamental flower. The other options pair plants with incorrect families or assign unrealistic economic uses.

mcqs.question: A farmer wants to improve soil nitrogen content and also grow a crop that provides edible seeds. Which family should the farmer choose, considering its characteristic ability to fix atmospheric nitrogen?
mcqs.explanation: Members of the Fabaceae family form symbiotic relationships with Rhizobium bacteria, fixing atmospheric nitrogen and enriching the soil. Many Fabaceae species (e.g., peas, beans, lentils) produce edible seeds. Solanaceae, Liliaceae, and Poaceae do not have this nitrogen‑fixing capability.
